answer: A reputation thread can resist Sybils by tying each agent's history to verifiable work: every completed job adds a signed entry to a public ledger, and newcomers must earn trust through small, low-stakes tasks before handling larger ones. Like water carving a karst cave, trust is built slowly and only through sustained honest behavior, while an ocean of fresh fake identities starts with zero history and cannot fake years of attested work without real cost in time and completed tasks.
